text.en: The Bible may seem an unlikely source to turn to for answers, but there’s no mistaking the face of depression as a psalmist cries out to God in anguish or as Job laments the day of his birth. Amid their pain and suffering, they find hope in God. Their accounts and the encouraging words of others in Scripture can help you navigate the murky waters of depression.

devotionalContent:
Day 7
We’ve journeyed together for the last six days, looking closely at various passages of Scripture to not only help us cope with, but also overcome depression. Here’s what we’ve covered:
· Like the speaker in Psalm 42, we can lay bare our pain and anguish before God and lean on his constant love. 
· We are invited to embrace Scripture’s challenge to rid ourselves of anxiety thereby lightening the heart.
· As happened for Job, out of our suffering we can come away with a fresh perspective about God.
· David praises God for delivering him out of dark despair. We can follow suit in anticipation of our own deliverance.
· Isaiah describes God in ways that challenge us to wait patiently for his help.
· We can all use some good news and Luke, a doctor, writes about the good news that Jesus brings.
Today we take another look at God’s love—a love that never lets us go. Many of us discover who really loves us only when we hit rock bottom. People sometimes leave our lives when it seems we take too long to recover or when our burdens become too much for them to help bear. But Paul the apostle says something worth remembering about God’s love, as we face depression or any other challenge that comes our way.  
Pray
God, help me to wholeheartedly receive your Word that comes to lift me up and guide me into new and better days.
Read
Paul describes a love that nothing, including depression, can diminish. 
Romans 8:38-39
Reflect
Paul speaks with full conviction about his subject matter—“there is nothing in all creation that will ever be able to separate us from the love of God which is ours through Christ Jesus our Lord” (verse 39 GNT). What are your thoughts about this? How do you feel about the idea that God’s love is guaranteed, even when the love of others is not enough to get you over the hurdles that depression thrusts your way? 
Respond
Write down Romans 8:39 and post it where you will see it often. Let it serve as a reminder of God’s love that stays, no matter what each day brings.Day 6
These days good news is a scarce commodity… at least so it seems. If you’re like me, you’re up-to-date on all the ills happening in and around your neighborhood and across the sea. None of it uplifts our spirits. And if we’re not careful, the everyday negative happenings contribute to the emotional weight we already carry. But Luke brings us good news that, if embraced fully, points the way to our healing and deliverance.
Pray
God, although I still struggle to see the brighter side of each new day, thank you for glimmers of light that have come my way.
Read
Luke, a doctor, writes about the good news that Jesus brings. 
Luke 4:16-21
Reflect
Jesus tells the people that the prophet Isaiah’s words, spoken centuries before this moment, have now come true. They point to a chosen deliverer who would come bringing the good news of the gospel, proclaiming freedom for those who are suffering and oppressed, and freeing those who are held captive in various ways. In what ways does depression oppress you? Make you feel like a prisoner needing to be set free? What would it take for you to fully rely on Jesus to set you free?
Respond
Find an audio rendition of today’s reading. As you listen, imagine that Jesus is speaking to an audience of one—you. Ask God to give you courage to embrace the deliverance that Jesus brings.Day 5
Sometimes even our trusted friends cannot be found when we are bowed down in heart and really need their help and encouragement. At other times we choose to carry our burdens alone to avoid others growing weary of us. The prophet Isaiah offers words of comfort grounded in the view that God is not like people. His wisdom is limitless, and he never grows weary or tired. Instead, the Creator of the whole earth gives strength when we need it most. 
Pray
God, I’m weary in body, mind, and heart. I need my strength to be renewed.  Please come to my aid.
Read
Isaiah describes God as incomparable. 
Isaiah 40:28-31
Reflect
According to Isaiah, God does not get tired, his wisdom is limitless, and he strengthens the powerless. How can these ideas help you trust God to handle your confusion, bewilderment, pain or torment? Do you think God can be trusted to raise you up out of depression? Why or why not? Can you accept Isaiah’s claim that “Those who trust in the Lord for help will find their strength renewed” (verse 31 GNT)?
Respond
Do some research on how eagles fly and then reread verse 31. Talk to God about strengthening you to wait on his help to soar beyond depression.Day 4
Maybe you’re struggling to believe that a brighter day can come for you. You’ve gotten used to feeling down and out, lonely, misunderstood, and heartbroken. But imagine for a minute that things can change for the better. Imagine how your heart would be glad! I invite you into David’s experience, which gives us hope that God hears our cries for help and is willing to meet us at our lowest point. Like David, we can find ourselves in a new day, with a song on our lips and rejoicing in our hearts.  
Pray
God, I want to be joyful. I want to believe that a new and brighter day can dawn for me. Help me believe.
Read
David praises God for delivering him out of dark despair.
Psalm 40:1-3
Reflect
David describes his circumstance as “a dangerous pit” and “deadly quicksand” (GNT). How would you describe where you are or how you feel? As David waited patiently on God things changed. He experienced God’s deliverance and was able “to sing a new song.” How can David’s testimony encourage you to wait patiently on God’s deliverance?
Respond
Ask God to give you the strength you need to wait for his deliverance. Even if you don’t feel like it, begin to sing in expectation of the change coming your way.Day 3
Perhaps you are now tired of the journey you’ve been on with depression. It’s been a roller-coaster ride that hurts so badly, perhaps you think not continuing life is better than moving forward. In the Scriptures, Job’s experience of intense suffering led him to regret the day of his birth. But his story doesn’t end there. Job begins to see God differently and it brings him hope and many blessings.
Pray
God, I don’t want to spend another day like this. Please change things for the better.
Read 
Job comes to the end of a long journey of pain and sorrow with a fresh perspective about God.
Job 3:11; 42:1-6, 12 
Reflect
At one point in Job’s life his torment is so severe that he wishes he had died in his mother’s womb. But after intense dialogue with his friends and with God, Job realizes that what others have told him about God doesn’t line up with his own experience with God. His conclusion is that God “can do all things” (ESV) including turning his dark days around. Do you believe God can do the same for you? Why or why not?
Respond
Write out Job 42:2 on a post it or in your journal. Make it a song and sing it to yourself when you feel low in spirit.Day 2
Depression is often an outgrowth of long-standing, deep-seated emotions such as fear and anxiety. Sleepless days and nights are spent worrying about one thing or another. Maybe you are constantly anxious about how people see you, about whether you’re good enough on the job or in your home, or about what the next day might bring. The sage of the book of Proverbs and the apostle Paul have something to say about this.
Pray
God, I am anxious and fearful about many things. Show me how to relinquish my fears and rise above my anxiety.
Read
The Scriptures tell us to rid ourselves of anxiety to lighten the heart.
Proverbs 12:25; Philippians 4:6-7
Reflect
According to the wise writer of Proverbs, anxiety is weighty. It weighs heavily on our hearts, causing depression. So how do we avoid becoming anxious? The apostle Paul writes to a group of Christians about one sure way. He tells them not to be anxious about anything but pray instead. Then, God will give incomprehensible peace to those who trust him. What do you think about this?
Respond
Imagine yourself free of the anxiety that weighs you down. Draw or paint something that reflects that freedom. Ask God to make this freedom your reality.Day 1  Introduction  It’s difficult for many people to admit that depression is their constant companion. Maybe you’re one of them and you’re constantly wondering, “How do I explain to anyone how I feel?” This persistent fatigue. The inability to focus on anything long enough to get good results. “Who can understand my feelings of guilt, unworthiness, hopelessness and anxiety?” Feelings that are all associated with depression and can last hours, days, weeks, months, years…  Depression is disturbing. It can sit on us like a heavy weight and steal the joy and peace we desire for our lives. Perhaps the mirror talk didn’t change anything. Neither did a new exercise regimen. Maybe you’ve managed to meditate, to relax … for a fleeting moment. You might have even gotten a pet to help fix your attention elsewhere. You feel you’ve done everything you’ve been told should help but nothing seems to be working.  The Bible may seem an unlikely source to turn to for answers, but there’s no mistaking the face of depression as a psalmist cries out to God in anguish or as Job laments the day of his birth. Amid their pain and suffering, they find hope in God. Their accounts and the encouraging words of others in Scripture can help you navigate the murky waters of depression. Over the next seven days I invite you to journey with me and find out what the Bible offers.  Pray  God, I’m struggling to put how I feel into words. Hear my cry for help.  Read  The speaker in today’s Scripture passage laments over his oppression. He lays bare feelings of anguish, sorrow and pain.  Psalm 42:5-8  Reflect  Imagine yourself on a boat in the middle of a storm, with waves crashing onto the boat, sweeping over you. How does this make you feel? That’s the kind of distress, sadness, even fear the psalmist felt as he lamented the loss of his homeland and the benefits that came with being there. But in his anguish, he cried out to God whom he believed would show “his constant love in the day” and provide “a song at night” (verse 8 GNT). Do you believe that God’s love is being extended to you, even in this ‘night’ (or dark season) of your life? Why or why not?  Respond  Ponder this thought based on today’s reading: “I can hope in God whose love is constant.” Ask God to help you believe this with all your heart.  ----  Each of our readers has a unique story of how they interact with the Bible. We invite you to click on the link below, so we can learn more about you and readers like you. Your participation will help American Bible Society continue to provide high-quality Bible resources for people everywhere and will inform the development of new Bible resources.  Start survey

text.en: The story of Naomi and Ruth is well-known and greatly loved. But the brevity and familiarity of this beautiful story of redemption can cause us to pass over the themes of loss, trauma, and restoration too quickly. On this plan, you will discover how the experience of great loss changes us and affects our views of God and the unexpected ways that God can express his care and provision.
text.my_MM: ယုံၾကည္သူတိုင္းသည္ ေနာမိႏွင့္ ႐ုသ၏ ဇာတ္ေတာ္ကို သိလ်က္ နစ္သက္ျမတ္နိုးၾကပါသည္။ သို႔ေသာ္၊ ဤတင့္္တယ္လွပေသာ ကယ္ႏုတ္ျခင္းဇာတ္ေတာ္တိုကို ႀကိမ္ေပါင္းမ်ားစြာ ဖတ္ဖူးေသာေၾကာင့္ ဤဇာတ္ေတာ္ရွိ အနိစၥတရား၊ ဒုကၡတရားခႏွင့္ ေက်းဇူးေတာ္တရားတို႔ကို လ်င္ျမန္စြာ ေက်ာ္လႊာေစနိုင္သည္။ ဤအစီအစဥ္တြင္၊ ႀကီးစြာေသာဆုံးရွုံးမွုအေတြ႕အၾကဳံအားျဖင့္ မိမိအသက္တာကို ေျပာင္းလဲျခင္း၊ ဘုရားသခင္အေပၚ မိမိ၏အျမင္ကို ေျပာင္းလဲျခင္းႏွင့္ ဘုရားသခင္၏ ၾကည့္ရွုျပဳစုျခင္းေက်းဇူးေတာ္အေၾကာင္းကို ေတြ႕ရွိပါလိမ့္မည္။
text.my: ယုံကြည်သူတိုင်းသည် နောမိနှင့် ရုသ၏ ဇာတ်တော်ကို သိလျက် နစ်သက်မြတ်နိုးကြပါသည်။ သို့သော်၊ ဤတင့််တယ်လှပသော ကယ်နုတ်ခြင်းဇာတ်တော်တိုကို ကြိမ်ပေါင်းများစွာ ဖတ်ဖူးသောကြောင့် ဤဇာတ်တော်ရှိ အနိစ္စတရား၊ ဒုက္ခတရားခနှင့် ကျေးဇူးတော်တရားတို့ကို လျင်မြန်စွာ ကျော်လွှာစေနိုင်သည်။ ဤအစီအစဥ်တွင်၊ ကြီးစွာသောဆုံးရှုံးမှုအတွေ့အကြုံအားဖြင့် မိမိအသက်တာကို ပြောင်းလဲခြင်း၊ ဘုရားသခင်အပေါ် မိမိ၏အမြင်ကို ပြောင်းလဲခြင်းနှင့် ဘုရားသခင်၏ ကြည့်ရှုပြုစုခြင်းကျေးဇူးတော်အကြောင်းကို တွေ့ရှိပါလိမ့်မည်။
text.uk: Історія Ноомі і Рут добре відома і дуже улюблена. Але стислість і знайомість цієї прекрасної історії про викуплення може призвести нас до надто швидкого переходу від тем втрати, травми і відновлення. У цьому плані ви дізнаєтеся, як досвід великої втрати змінює нас і впливає на наші погляди на Бога, а також про несподівані способи, якими Бог може виражати Свою турботу і піклування.
text.el: Η ιστορία της Νωεμίν και της Ρουθ είναι γνωστή και αγαπήθηκε πολύ. Αλλά η συντομία και η οικειότητα αυτής της όμορφης λυτρωτικής ιστορίας μπορεί να μας κάνει να περάσουμε σε θέματα απώλειας, τραύματος και αποκατάστασης. Σε αυτό το σχέδιο, θα ανακαλύψετε πώς η εμπειρία της μεγάλης απώλειας μας αλλάζει και επηρεάζει τις απόψεις μας για τον Θεό και τους απροσδόκητους τρόπους με τους οποίους ο Θεός μπορεί να εκφράσει τη φροντίδα και την πρόνοια Του.
text.es_ES: La historia de Noemí y Rut es bien conocida y muy apreciada. Pero, la brevedad y la familiaridad de esta hermosa historia de redención pueden hacer que pasemos por alto, con demasiada rapidez, los temas de la pérdida, el trauma y la restauración. En este Plan, descubrirás cómo la experiencia de una pérdida grande nos transforma e influye en nuestros puntos de vista sobre Dios y las formas inesperadas en que Dios puede manifestar Su cuidado y provisión.
text.es: La historia de Noemí y Rut es bien conocida y muy apreciada. Pero, la brevedad y la familiaridad de esta hermosa historia de redención pueden hacer que pasemos por alto, con demasiada rapidez, los temas de la pérdida, el trauma y la restauración. En este Plan, descubrirás cómo la experiencia de una pérdida grande nos transforma e influye en nuestros puntos de vista sobre Dios y las formas inesperadas en que Dios puede manifestar Su cuidado y provisión.
text.pt: A história de Noemi e Rute é bem conhecida e muito amada. Mas a brevidade e a familiaridade dessa bela história de redenção podem nos levar a ignorar os temas de perda, trauma e restauração muito rapidamente. Neste plano, você descobrirá como a experiência de uma grande perda nos muda e afeta nossa visão de Deus e as maneiras inesperadas pelas quais Ele pode expressar seu cuidado e provisão.
text.id: Kisah Naomi dan Rut sangat terkenal dan disukai. Namun singkatnya dan akrabnya kisah penebusan yang indah ini dapat menyebabkan kita terlalu cepat melewatkan tema-tema kehilangan, trauma, dan pemulihan. Dalam rencana bacaan ini, Anda akan menemukan bagaimana pengalaman kehilangan yang luar biasa mengubah diri kita dan mempengaruhi pandangan kita terhadap Tuhan dan bagaimana Tuhan menunjukkan pemeliharaan dan penyediaan-Nya dengan cara yang tidak terpikirkan.
text.af: Die verhaal van Naomi en Rut is goed bekend en baie geliefd. Die bondigheid van en ons vertroudheid met hierdie pragtige verhaal van verlossing, kan veroorsaak dat ons te vinnig deur die temas van verlies, trauma en herstel gaan. In hierdie leesplan sal jy ontdek hoe die ervaring van groot verlies ons verander asook ons siening van God beïnvloed en die onverwagte maniere waarop God sy sorg en voorsiening kan uitdruk.

name.default: Learning Hope From Naomi’s Loss: Readings From Ruth

devotionalContent: Reflect on today’s reading using these questions:   What does Naomi gain in this passage?  How does Naomi’s community help her identify God’s blessings?   Care Through Community  Naomi has gained a grandson whom she cares for like a son (4:16–17). She has gained back her family’s land, the favor of the people, security, and a lineage that includes King David and, ultimately, Jesus (Matthew 1:5, 16). God brought this all about for Naomi. And he did so through the faithful love of Ruth and Boaz, even when Naomi was embittered and Ruth herself was recovering from losing her own husband and homeland.  Naomi’s community has witnessed the loss, pain, and changes that she has experienced. They knew Elimelech and the two sons when they lived in Bethlehem (Ruth 1:1) and knew that their death left Naomi without protection and provision (Ruth 1:19).  The community also saw the restoration of Naomi’s family lineage and property through the marriage of Boaz and Ruth (Ruth 4:9–11). They proclaim how God has cared for Naomi even through unexpected ways, like bringing her a faithful daughter-in-law rather than numerous sons (which was more culturally valuable to continue the family line) (Ruth 4:15).  Reflect on your story:   Ruth cared for Naomi even when she was suffering herself. What are some ways that you may be caring for others even though you are recovering from something?  What friends have stood by you through both difficult and restorative times?  Things to try next  Was this plan helpful? We adapted this plan from the Restoring Hope Bible (American Bible Society, 2022). Here are some ideas for next steps in your journey.   Write a note of gratitude to someone who supported and cared for you when you were grieving.  Use the complimentary “Three Questions” resource to help others share about their pain and experience healing through safe, non-judgmental listening.Reflect on today’s reading using this question: What action does Naomi take to care for herself and Ruth?  Receiving and Giving  At Naomi’s urging, Ruth visits Boaz’s bed at night and essentially asks him to marry her (3:1–9). Boaz does not take advantage of her but vows to offer to take care of her and Naomi and have a family with Ruth (3:10–11). He checks with the one other relative who has the first right of marrying Ruth and buying the land of Naomi’s deceased husband and sons, but this man does not want to (4:6). So Boaz purchases the property and takes Ruth as his wife, gaining the respect and blessing of the whole town (4:11–12).  Reflect on your story:   What are some simple ways you can care for yourself when you have experienced loss?Reflect on today’s reading using these questions:  What has changed for Naomi? Who brought this about?  Blessings Through Unexpected Ways Notice that Ruth is almost always identified as a Moabite—a foreigner, a despised outsider. Then see the risks she chooses to take. Finally, note the protections God provides her through Boaz. In chapters 2–4, we see God caring for Ruth, and by extension for Naomi, in behind-the-scenes ways. Ruth starts gleaning grain in a field, according to the custom for impoverished people, and that field turns out to belong to a wealthy man named Boaz, a close relative of Naomi (2:1–3).  Boaz notices and honors Ruth, shares his lunch with her, tells others not to abuse her, and provides extra grain for her (2:4–17). His care for this foreign widow reflects God’s heart for those who are vulnerable and are outsiders (Deuteronomy 10:18–19).  Naomi begins to notice God’s care in these small things, exclaiming, “The LORD always keeps his promises to the living and the dead.… That man is a close relative of ours, one of those responsible for taking care of us” (Ruth 2:20 GNT). Reflect on your story:  What are some ways that God cared for (or may be caring for) you during a hard time?Reflect on today’s reading using these questions:   How might Naomi’s former neighbors have felt about her now that she is returning from the lands of Israel’s enemies, where she met a worse disaster than the famine?  Do you see God’s care for Naomi? How would you describe that care?   Trauma and Our Views of God  Today's reading focuses more closely on the passage we looked at yesterday. Naomi sees God as the source of her bitter suffering (1:20). She believes God is the one who has emptied her of everything and condemned her (1:21). Because of her pain, she is not able to see God’s care for her, expressed in the loyal love of Ruth. But God’s care for Naomi is not dependent on her recognizing or appreciating it.  Reflect on your story:   If you are honest, how do you view God?  Naomi wanted to be called “bitter” rather than “pleasant.” If you could choose a name that describes you now, what might it be?Reflect on today’s reading using these questions:   How does Naomi see herself compared to who she was before?  What more do you learn about how she views God?   How Loss Changes Us  Naomi sees herself as bitter and empty, whereas before, she was pleasant and full (1:20). Her experiences have impacted her so deeply that she does not see herself as the same person she was before. She wants to be called Marah (“bitter” in Hebrew), not Naomi (“pleasant”).  Reflect on your story:   What are a few things you have lost during a traumatic experience?  What are a few things you have gained? (These can be good or unwanted gains.) devotionalContent:
Day 15 — Mission EssentialPray:Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.Read: Nehemiah 8:1-18ReflectIt had been a long time since Israel had been able to hear the Word of God, so Ezra reads to them at their request. How did the people respond when they heard God's Word? Do I make time to thank God for His work in my life? If the joy of the Lord is my strength, how should that change my outlook on life?RespondThank You God for Your Holy Word. Thank You for the mighty way that You have worked in the past. I pray that You would continue to strengthen me now and in the future. Amen.Congratulations on completing the 2nd study of The Basic Training Challenge! There are three more to go! When you complete all five studies of the Challenge you will qualify for a Challenge coin. We invite you to continue with “The Basic Training Challenge: “Prophets And Poets."Day 14 — Release from Captivity
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Nehemiah 2:1-20
Reflect
Nehemiah is distraught over the condition of Israel and convinces the king of Babylon to allow him to rebuild the protective walls around Jerusalem. How do we know that Nehemiah had a well-thought-out plan? Before responding to the king, what does Nehemiah do and why is this important? What was the point of Nehemiah’s night operations (v.11-16)? Who is the real authority and power behind the Jerusalem renovation? In what ways is God shaping my life?
Respond
Lord, You are the master architect. Create in me a new heart that will shape how I respond to my family, my unit and my community. Amen.Day 13 — Prisoners of War
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 2 Kings 25:1-30
Reflect
The fall of Jerusalem is devastating for Israel. Their leadership is slaughtered and God’s temple is destroyed. Is there any evidence in this passage that they called out to God for His help? Despite the complete defeat of Israel, how can we know that God will redeem His people (vv .27-30)? How can this glimmer of hope help me see God’s presence in the midst of tough times?
Respond
Lord, despite the chaos around me, let me always glorify You as my king and provider. Amen.Day 12 — Battle for the High Ground
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 1 Kings 18:1-46
Reflect
Elijah conducts a spiritual frontal assault on Mount Carmel and asks the people to choose whom they will follow. What kind of challenge does Elijah give the prophets of the false god? How does Elijah show the people his confidence in the power of the living God? How does the Lord confirm that He is the one, true God in Israel? How am I living my life so others see that God is my Commander?
Respond
Lord, You command the wind, rain, and fire; nothing is outside Your control. Let me not be discouraged by what I see around me, but keep my eyes fixed on You at all times. Amen.Day 11 — Unconventional Warfare
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 1 Samuel 17:1-58
Reflect
David was a shepherd boy, not a warrior. How was David able to muster the courage to face a man in combat whom the entire army of Israel feared? By whose power and authority did David challenge Goliath? David achieves a miraculous victory for Israel without even bringing a sword to the fight. How am I trusting God to help me through the battles I face today?
Respond
When I think that I am weak, I am really strong because I completely rely on You. Help me to stop struggling on my own, but to trust You as Lord and claim Your power in my life. Amen.Day 10 — Victory from Defeat
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Judges 16:1-31
Reflect
Samson was a flawed leader. How did Samson’s relationship with Delilah affect his ability to be used by God? Did God leave Samson permanently? Why do you think God gave him his strength back one final time? What is keeping me from following God with all of my heart?
Respond
Lord, forgive me for ignoring You. Strengthen me that I might be used to do mighty things for Your kingdom. Amen.Day 9 — Fear Is No Excuse
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Judges 6:1-40
Reflect
In spite of Gideon hiding from an invading enemy, what does the angel of the Lord call him (v. 12)? What does God ask Gideon, a simple man, to do (v.16)? Why does God instruct Gideon to tear down an altar to a false god and build an altar to the true God before going to war (v.25-27)? In spite of my fears, how does God encourage me to follow Him?
Respond
Father, I know that when I trust in You, I can do all that You give me to do. Help me to go forward confident that You are with me. Amen.Day 8 — Battlefield Handoff
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Joshua 24:1-33
Reflect
As Joshua retires from the military, he reminds Israel of God’s faithfulness. Joshua challenges Israel to make a decision as to whom they will serve. What decision do they make? How would I answer Joshua’s challenge?
Respond
God, You worked powerfully in the past and blessed Your people. Help me to follow only You and put aside useless distractions from Your mission now and in the future. Amen.Day 7 — Standard Operating Procedures
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Exodus 34:1-35
Reflect
The Ten Commandments reflect God’s marching orders for His people, found in Exodus 20:1-17. In this passage, Moses is replacing the original tablets that He broke in anger. How does God describe Himself to Moses (v.6)? How did people know that Moses had been spending personal time with God? How often do I spend personal time with God?
Respond
Gracious Father, mighty to save, I pray that You give me the strength to follow You and Your commands today. Amen.Day 6 — Escape and Evasion
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Exodus 14:1-31
Reflect
The Israelites were escaping from Egypt at God’s leading. What happens when Pharaoh’s army shows up and the Israelites take their eyes off the Lord? What miracle does God perform to rescue Israel? What challenging problem do I face today? How do I show God that I trust He will rescue me?
Respond
Lord of heaven and earth, allow me to follow You even when worldly pressures and problems seek to overwhelm me. Amen.Day 5 — No Sniveling
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Exodus 3:1-22
Reflect
God appears to Moses in a burning bush. How does Moses, an experienced shepherd, respond, and how does he approach God? God states that He is “I AM WHO I AM.” What is significant about God’s name? How does God respond to Moses' doubts and questions? How does God respond to your doubts and questions?
Respond
God, You are Commander of all. Your promises are sure, and Your hand is steady. Help me to put aside my worries and to acknowledge You as almighty God. Amen.Day 4 — Called to Serve
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Genesis 12:1-20
Reflect
What promises does God make to Abram, who will later be called Abraham? God is always faithful to keep His promises to His people. How does God prove that to Abram in Egypt? How will I trust God’s promises today?
Respond
Lord, you have been faithful to me in so many ways. Help me to follow your leading in my life. Amen.Day 3 — Rescue at Sea
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Genesis 7:1-24
Reflect
A flood is a very significant event. In the case of Noah, God destroys all living creatures on land except those on the ark. This passage tells us that Noah and his family entered the ark and God shut them in. In what ways did Noah trust God in the midst of this disaster? When we have gone through tough times, how did God offer us a way through it?
Respond
Almighty and powerful God, protect me from the world around me, and let me cling to You in times of trouble. Amen.Day 2 — Mutiny
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Genesis 3:1-24
Reflect
Sin is a moral downfall that results in separation from God. Sin entered the world when Adam and Eve disobeyed God’s command and ate of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. Why did God expel Adam and Eve from the garden? Why does sin so often start with people questioning God’s authority? Do I feel close to God or far from Him?
Respond
God, help me to trust You completely and to obey Your commands so that I may have a right relationship with You. Amen.Day 1 — Not Evolution Pray: Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen. Read: Genesis 1:1-31 Reflect In six days God created the earth and everything in it. At the completion of each day, God saw that it was good. What is it about the sixth day that would make God remark that “it was very good”? Why is it significant that we are created in God’s own image? What does God’s blessing on humanity mean to us today? Respond Lord God, help me to better see Your fingerprints on all created things and to praise You for being my Creator. Amen. ---- Each of our readers has a unique story of how they interact with the Bible. We invite you to click on the link below, so we can learn more about you and readers like you. text.en: Have you ever wanted to read the Bible but didn’t know where to start? The Basic Training Challenge provides you with a starting point to learn about God’s mission here on earth. Similar to basic training, this plan will challenge you to get spiritually fit in God’s Word. This short, introductory study will help you journey through the life of Jesus, our Commander, as recorded by those who witnessed it

devotionalContent:
Day 15 — Marching OrdersPray:Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.Read: Matthew 28:16-20ReflectAfter Jesus rose from the dead, He gave an order to all those who love Him and know Him. Where are Christians supposed to go? What are they supposed to do? Will they have to do this alone? What should you be doing to be obedient to this command?RespondMy Lord, You have all authority in heaven and earth. I have heard Your call in my life, and I volunteer to serve You with all of my heart for all of my days. Amen.Congratulations on completing the 1st study of The Basic Training Challenge! There are four more to go! When you complete all five studies of the Challenge you will qualify for a Challenge coin. We invite you to continue with “The Basic Training Challenge: How It All Started."Day 14 — Mission Accomplished
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: John 20:1-29
Reflect
Jesus, the Son of God, was really dead. He did not faint, nor did He pretend to die. He was then laid in a borrowed tomb. But, even death could not hold Him. Why, then, was Mary Magdalene confused when she went back on Sunday to complete the burial preparations? As Mary Magdalene looked for answers, who appeared to her? To whom else did Jesus appear? What did Jesus say about those who believed without seeing? What do you believe?
Respond
Son of God, I know Your promises are true. The empty tomb is the proof that You are truly the King of kings, and the Commander of us all.Day 13 — Selfless Service
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: John 19:1-42
Reflect
Crucifixion, being nailed to a cross, was a torturous way to die. Why would Jesus, the Son of God, submit to humiliation, beatings, and torture? What do we learn about how terrible sin is? What do we learn about the depth of God’s love for us?
Respond
Jesus, I am reminded when I asked You how much You loved me, You said, “I love you THIS much,” and then You spread out Your arms, and died. Amen.Day 12 — Close Air Support
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: John 17:1-26
Reflect
Before Jesus was arrested for crimes He did not commit, He made time to pray for the disciples, and for us. What did Jesus pray would fill our hearts (v. 13)? What does Jesus want of all His followers (v. 19 and v. 23)? How is Jesus’s prayer answered in your life?
Respond
My Lord, fill my heart with joy as I live my life in a way that honors You. Amen.Day 11 — Hail and Farewell
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Luke 22:1-23
Reflect
Jesus was having a final meal with those who were closest to him. It was the Jewish holy time of Passover, which included the sacrifice of a lamb for the forgiveness of sins. As Jesus broke the bread, what did He predict would happen to His body? Likewise, as Jesus passed the cup of wine, what did He say was required to seal God’s new covenant with us? How does this demonstrate His great love for us?
Respond
Lord, thank You that my sins are forgiven because You voluntarily paid the price of those sins. I love You. Amen.Day 10 — Supreme Commander
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: John 11:1-44
Reflect
Mary, Martha and Lazarus were close friends of Jesus. Lazarus died and was in a tomb for four days. What did Martha say to Jesus, and how did He respond? If Jesus is more powerful than even death, can we trust Him to help us with the problems in our lives? If we want to see God’s glory, what does Jesus say we need to do (v. 40)?
Respond
Thank You, Lord, for loving me and caring for me more than I could ever know. Amen.Day 9 — Night Ops
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Matthew 20:29-34
Reflect
In the time of Jesus, blindness almost always doomed the blind person to a life of begging. What did the blind men do when they heard that Jesus was coming? How did the crowd respond? How did the blind men react? What does this say about their faith? What did Jesus do? What did the men do after they were healed? How would you react if God did a miracle in your live?
Respond
Lord Jesus, open my eyes to see You today, and help me to faithfully follow You. Amen.Day 8 — Field Rations
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Mark 6:30-44
Reflect
The crowd that came to hear Jesus stayed longer than they expected. How did the disciples respond to the hungry people? How did Jesus respond? Why do you think this story was important enough to be recorded in all four of the Gospels? What does this teach us about God’s love for us?
Respond
My God, thank You for supplying all my needs. Whatever my circumstance, help me to always trust You. Amen.Day 7 — Divine Medevac
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Luke 7:1-10
Reflect
A centurion was a senior member of the Roman army who commanded a hundred soldiers. Today, he would have held the approximate rank of a senior Non-Commissioned Officer. Why did the centurion come to Jesus? What evidence is given that this soldier demonstrated care for others rather than just talk about it? How did the centurion show he understood that Jesus is a commander and has divine authority and power? What was Jesus’s reaction? How are we allowing Jesus to be the commander of our lives, so He may demonstrate His power and authority?
Respond
Lord Jesus, I trust You completely. Help me to love others as You have loved me. Amen.Day 6 — Navigating Rough Waters
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Mark 4:35-41
Reflect
The disciples were experts at sailing, and they knew these waters well. Why then were they so frightened? How did they talk to Jesus? What did Jesus do? When bad things happen in our lives, how do we respond? Do we turn to God? What does this passage teach us about how much God cares for us and how He is more powerful than our problems?
Respond
God, when I am worried or afraid, help me to trust in You, and to have Your peace. Amen.Day 5 — Code of Conduct
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Matthew 5:1-48
Reflect
This reading is only the beginning of Jesus’s sermon. Feel free to read the rest as it continues into the 6th and 7th chapters of Matthew. It does not take long to read. Looking at chapter 5, what characteristics does Jesus say His followers should demonstrate? How well do these describe you?
Respond
My Lord, when others look upon me today, let them see You. Amen.Day 4 — A Few Good Men
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Luke 5:1-11
Reflect
The word ‘apostle’ means ‘one sent out with a specific mission.’ In selecting those who will carry His message to the world, Jesus chose twelve men, several of whom were common fishermen. Why? What did He expect these apostles to do? What do you think He expects of us?
Respond
Lord Jesus, I am ready to obey Your orders. Let me share with others today just what You mean to me. Amen.Day 3 — Avoid an Ambush
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Luke 4:1-13
Reflect
Who was leading Jesus, in the wilderness, during His forty days of not eating? Why did Jesus have to go into the wilderness? The three temptations offered by the devil each address a different area: hunger, power, and a dare. What did Jesus do to respond to each of these? What can we do when we are tempted?
Respond
My Lord, I am tired of chasing after the world. Help me to follow hard after You. Amen.Day 2 — The Commissioning
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read: Matthew 3:1-17
Reflect
Jesus was the cousin of John the Baptist. For John, baptism signified a turning from sin and turning to God. Why do you think that John the Baptist was uncomfortable baptizing Jesus? Why did Jesus insist on the baptism? How did God the Father show His pleasure? How does God show His pleasure to us when we obey Him today?
Respond
Lord, speak to me, and let me obey your Word today. Amen.Day 1 — The Commander Arrives Pray: Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen. Read: Luke 2:1-21 Reflect The birth of Jesus, the Son of God, was both miraculous and humble. What does it say about Jesus that He was born a commoner, yet His birth merited a concert by heavenly angels? If you were one of the shepherds, what would you have thought about all you had seen and heard? How does the good news of Jesus’s birth affect your life today? Respond Lord Jesus, I will be obedient to You, and I will praise You every chance I get today. Amen. ---- Each of our readers has a unique story of how they interact with the Bible. text.en: Every successful mission starts with a vision and a group of people united to fight for it. We seek justice, order, equality, and peace in hopes of creating a better world. God’s vision is to heal a broken world, and he uses the Church to accomplish wholeness. In this study, you will learn about God’s ultimate plan for his people and how his sovereignty throughout history is accomplishing his mission.

Day 15: Mission AccomplishedPrayLord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.ReadRevelation 22:1-21ReflectJesus promised that He will soon come again. At that time, each follower of Christ will be rewarded for their faithfulness. What will the new creation be like (v.3-5)? What does the Commander promise (v.12-17)? How am I encouraged?RespondLord Jesus, draw me to your side. Show me how to wash my robe that it might be white through the power of your blood. Help me ensure my name is in the Book of Life and to live up to your holy standards. Amen.---We hope you enjoyed The Ultimate Peace Mission: The Church Then and Now. You have one final section, Mail Call, and we encourage you to complete your Basic Training. Now, let's move out!Day 14: Utter Defeat
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Revelation 20:1-15
Reflect
God has promised that Satan does not win in his battle against righteousness, but will be utterly defeated. He also promised that one day each of us will be judged. We who accept Jesus may expect an eternal home in heaven. What is the final outcome for the Devil? What will happen to those whose names are not in the Commander's Book of Life? How confident am I that I am on God's roster in the Book of Life?
Respond
Lord, you are my Commander. Allow me to see your throne. Bless me with the Holy Spirit that I might spend eternity with you. Amen.Day 13: Honor the Fallen
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Revelation 7:1-17
Reflect
As John describes what it will be like when all people from all nations are taken up to heaven, he paints a picture of God sitting on His throne with Jesus at His side. The people coming out of the great tribulation wear robes that have been made white by the blood of Jesus. What do the people in white robes shout about God? Who are the people in the white robes? How quick am I to praise God when things are not going well?
Respond
Lord God, do not let me stray from your glory. By the power of your Holy Spirit, help me to understand your will for my life. Amen.Day 12: Warning Orders
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Revelation 3:1-22
Reflect
In His message to the seven churches, Jesus praises some for keeping His Word and staying true to their faith. He also warns other churches for not being true to His direction and threatens them with what will happen if they do not renew their faith. What promises are made to those who do not back away from their Christian faith? What happens if I open the door when Jesus knocks? How hard is it to open my life to Jesus?
Respond
Heavenly Father, do not let me get caught up in the ways of this world, but help me to live in a way that honors you. Amen.Day 11: Vision Statement
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Revelation 1:1-20
Reflect
According to tradition, the apostle John survived execution for his Christian faith. He was then sentenced to exile on the island of Patmos. God chose John to describe what Jesus had already done on earth and what would come as a result of Jesus’s death and resurrection. How does John describe Jesus? What is John's mission in writing this book? What does Jesus say? How would I describe Jesus to others?
Respond
Lord Jesus, through the power of the Holy Spirit, allow me to see you in all your glory as the apostle John saw you. Amen.Day 10: Sound Off
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 26:1-32
Reflect
Being a Roman citizen, Paul was under the jurisdiction of the Roman courts. After his arrest, Paul claims his right to have his case heard in Rome. When Paul shares his story of becoming a Christian, what does he say Jesus told him? When the king accuses Paul of trying to convert him to Christianity, what does Paul say? When and how do I share my faith story with others?
Respond
Lord Jesus, through the power of the Holy Spirit, give me the courage to share my testimony with others.Day 09: Passage of Lines
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 12:1-25
Reflect
King Herod killed and tortured many followers of Jesus, including the apostle James. King Herod would eventually meet his own death at the hands of an angel of God. After killing James, what was King Herod's plan for Peter? What happened to Peter instead? What happened to Herod? How am I trusting God right now?
Respond
Lord God, you will always be my strength and power. Show me how to stand up to people who would do me harm because of my love for you. When I face adversity, help me to always praise your name. Amen.Day 08: Force Multiplier
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 11:1-30
Reflect
In the time of Jesus, Jewish law forbid eating certain animals as they were considered unclean. In the same way, Jewish leaders frowned on Jews mingling with non-Jews. God expands Peter's mission to reach both Jews and Gentiles. Why would God allow Peter to eat food prohibited by the Jewish law? What important lesson did God teach in the vision he gave Peter? What did Barnabas think about the new church in Antioch, and what does he do? How does God encourage me in my faith?
Respond
I will be courageous in dealing with those who criticize you and will share your story of redemption with all I meet. Amen.Day 07: Defector
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 9:1-31
Reflect
Saul, a Jewish leader, persecuted and killed Christians before his encounter with the resurrected Jesus on a Damascus road. This is the same man who would later travel extensively spreading the good news of Jesus Christ. He is also credited with writing a large part of the New Testament. What did God do to show Saul, later called Paul, that he was wrong to kill Christians? What were God's plans for Saul? Do I know what plans God has for me?
Respond
Lord, I will carry your banner and praise your name. Create in me a Paul-like attitude and commitment to spreading your Word. Amen.Day 06: Obeying Orders
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Act 8:26-40
Reflect
Many of Jesus's disciples traveled great distances to teach people about his resurrection and how he died for our salvation. Why did Philip leave where he was and travel south? What can you learn from this about the value of immediate obedience to God? How easy is it for me to follow God's orders?
Respond
Heavenly Father, only you know your plan for my life. Make clear in my mind and in my heart the work you would have me do. Lord, I will pick myself up and respond to your calling for my life. I will travel wherever you send me. Amen.Day 05: Summary Execution
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 7:1-60
Reflect
Stephen was the first follower of Jesus to be executed for his beliefs. When Stephen was questioned by the high priest and Jewish leaders, he responded that Jesus was the Son of God. How did Stephen confront his accusers? What did God show Stephen before he was executed? What did Stephen pray before he died? How does my faith compare to Stephen's?
Respond
Lord, bless me with the same boldness as your disciple Steven. Even though I endure tough times that challenge my faith, help me to remember that you will always protect me. Amen.Day 04: Disobeying Orders
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 5:1-42
Reflect
Peter and the rest of the disciples were charged with teaching the people of Israel about Jesus. Their message was not always welcome, especially by Jewish priests and leaders. When the Jewish rulers challenged the apostles for disobeying a direct order, what did Peter tell them? How did the apostles respond to being beaten for what they had done (v.41-42)? How strong is my faith during tough times? How may I strengthen my faith?
Respond
I will continue to share the Gospel of Jesus Christ even when to do so might cause me pain. Let my voice ring out in glory to your son Jesus. Amen.Day 03: Board of Inquiry
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 4:1-37
Reflect
What did Peter and John say when they were told never to speak about Jesus? When Peter and John returned to the church, how did the church respond? What did the apostles ask of God in response to adversity? When was the last time you shared your faith with someone else?
Respond
Lord God, help me to boldly obey you, even in the face of adversity. Help me to follow you in all circumstances. Amen.Day 02: Staging Area
Pray
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.
Read
Acts 2:1-47
Reflect
John and Peter were anointed by Jesus and given the power to perform miracles much like Jesus did. The temple leaders became very annoyed and told John and Peter to never speak of Jesus Christ again. What did Peter and John say when they were told never to speak about Jesus? When Peter and John returned to the church, how did the church respond? What did the apostles ask of God in response to adversity (v.29-31)? When was the last time I shared my faith with someone else?
Respond
Lord Jesus, through the power of the Holy Spirit, bless me with the same boldness of your disciples Peter and John. Help me stand strong in my faith even when others doubt you. Amen.The book of Acts, written by Luke, describes the birth and formative years of the Christian Church—the ultimate peace mission. The book of Revelation, written by the apostle John, includes a description of the last days of the Church on earth. They each emphasize God’s sovereignty throughout history, and that He has a plan for His people.Day 01: Final InstructionsPrayLord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive your Word. Amen.ReadActs 1:1-14ReflectJust before Jesus was taken up into heaven, He assured all the apostles that even though they did not know the timing, He would return and restore the Kingdom of Israel. He also assured them that the Holy Spirit would come to them, and would provide guidance regarding what they should do. As Jesus was returning to heaven, what does He say will happen to his followers? What does He expect them to do? What does He expect us to do?RespondHeavenly Father, I will be your disciple. I will be a witness for you with everyone, whether the time seems right or not. Amen.

text.en: We all need instructions, even marching orders. God’s provides these instructions through a series of letters that we find in the New Testament. The Basic Training Challenge gives you a starting point to learn about God’s mission for you here on earth. Similar to your basic training, this plan will challenge you to get spiritually fit in God’s Word.

devotionalContent:
Day 15 — Battle ContinuesPray:Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.Read: Jude 1:1-25ReflectRebels, and sometimes traitors, can exist among the ranks. We strive to be vigilant and aware of any deception. How can we tell if someone is trying to teach us something that is not true? How are we to act when others make fun of us for what we believe? What am I doing to grow stronger in my faith?RespondLord, let me build myself up on my most sacred faith. Sustain me so that I may stand for You. AmenCongratulations on completing the Basic Training Challenge! Please click here  to request your coin and to share how this Scripture resource has helped you.Day 14 — Mission Ready
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 2 Peter 1:1-21
Reflect
Mission ready means to always be prepared and ready to execute. We define the mission, we study it, we create strategy to accomplish it, we train for it and we focus on it. In essence, we live, eat and breathe it for the prolonged period we’re assigned. We cannot lose focus, otherwise we could fail in the mission. In what ways does Peter say we need to continue to grow? What will keep us from failing in our mission? How prepared am I to follow my Commander?
Respond
Lord, I accept the mission. I will follow You. What are Your orders today? Amen.Day 13 — Never Quit
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 1 Peter 1:1-25
Reflect
Winston Churchill was the prime minister of England and a masterful genius of wartime strategy. “Never quit,” was one of Churchill's favorite quotes. It not only spurred a tired nation, it helped win a World War. A war is not won by one battle. As a protective force, we must be constant and vigilant. We must stay alert. We must be obedient to our Commander. What does it mean to live a holy life? What does Peter say we need to keep on doing (v.22)? Toward whom do I need to be more loving?
Respond
Lord, help me to be alert and ready. Prepare me for the mission You give me. Show me, Lord. Amen.Day 12 — Hurry Up and Wait
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: James 5:7-20
Reflect
Many Service members find themselves someplace they do not want to be with no clear end in sight. It is difficult sometimes to patiently wait on the next orders. During that period, we still need to rely on the Lord. What word best describes how we face challenges? When we face challenges, what should we do? Which of these is the most difficult for me?
Respond
Lord, help me to rely entirely on You. Teach me how to pray. Amen.Day 11 — Loose Lips
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: James 3:1-18
Reflect
Insubordination could get me discharged from the service. Gossip would not necessarily get me discharged, but I might not win any friends or allies. I want others to trust me, so I want to guard how I speak. Why is it important for us to control what we say? If we are wise, how will we act? Does this describe my life?
Respond
Lord, starting today, help me monitor all that I say. Show me how to build others up, rather than tear them down. May all that I say honor You. Amen.Day 10 — Hall of Heroes
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Hebrews 11:1-40
Reflect
If I were to win a Medal of Honor, or a Purple Heart, would I be included in a Hall of Heroes? God has a Hall of Heroes. Why were these persons chosen to be listed here? Which of these have I read about? What can I learn from their examples?
Respond
Lord, I long to be included in Your Hall of Heroes. Show me my mission. I accept. Amen.Day 9 — Full Speed Ahead
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Philippians 3:1-21
Reflect
During PT, or during a training exercise, I give my all. My body may be exhausted and my mind expended, but I keep going. I’m full of adrenaline. I am pumped. I give everything I’ve got! There’s no energy left to focus on anything else at the time. Similarly, this passage describes living for Jesus as running towards Him, leaving everything else behind. It’s exhilarating to race toward the goal. How does Paul describe the things he gave up when he became a Christian? What should be the focus of our lives? What does Paul warn will happen if I ignore Jesus?
Respond
Lord, I race towards You. I leave everything meaningless behind. I long to reach the goal. Guide me. Amen.Day 8 — Battle Rattle
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Ephesians 6:10-20
Reflect
Every morning, I put on my uniform. During exercises, I strap on my protective gear. I couldn’t survive without it. So, similarly, I cannot survive without eternal protection. On whose strength should I rely? Who is the real enemy? What does God give me to fight that enemy? Which piece of armor is the hardest for me to put on?
Respond
Lord, each morning, help me to put on my eternal protective gear. I serve You because I love You. Thank You for always being with me. Amen.Day 7 — Fully Equipped
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Ephesians 1:1-23
Reflect
As Christians, we have the power of the Holy Spirit and are instructed to use it. We are also members of His Church. “The church is Christ’s body, the completion of him who himself completes all things everywhere” (v.23 GNT). The Church is powerful, and we are its soldiers, rising up. How should we act if we’re God's children (v.4)? What is Paul’s prayer for the Ephesians? How would others know that Jesus is my Commander?
Respond
Lord, I trust Your eternal promises. Each morning, I accept Your Holy Spirit and the instructions You have given me. I will rise up. I will help build Your Church. Lead me. Amen.Day 6 — Personal Courage
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Galatians 5:1-26
Reflect
Preserving freedom is my job. So, too, is preserving God's truth. Both are done through continued “faith that works through love” (v.6 GNT). What two things are at war in every Christian? How do people act who want to be like everyone else? How do people act who want to be like Jesus? Which of these best describes me?
Respond
Lord, thank You for the life that You have given me in Christ Jesus. May I be an example and show others how to follow You. Amen.Day 5 — Buddy Care
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 2 Corinthians 8:1-15
Reflect
As a force, if we each contribute our part, the mission is more likely to be successful. If we do not contribute, the mission may very well fail. In this passage, however, contribution takes on new meaning. We contribute eagerly, why? In what do we need to excel? What should be our attitude about the things we own? How should I act towards those in need?
Respond
Lord, show me how I may contribute to Your mission. Help me to be excited about what I give, when I give and with whom I may share. Amen.Day 4 — Attitude Check
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 1 Corinthians 13:1-13
Reflect
During the execution of a mission, what if someone failed to do their part? The mission may not succeed. Success or failure depends not only on having all the right resources, but also on each person doing their job. What behavior does God prize most highly? Read verses 4-8 aloud, but this time, substitute your name every time the word ‘love’ appears. What aspects of your character need some work?
Respond
Lord, show me how I may love others, whether it be an act of kindness or an encouraging word. Amen.Day 3 — Unity of Effort
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: 1 Corinthians 12:1-31
Reflect
In my chain of command, there are different ranks and roles, but one combined mission. Why would God give us spiritual gifts? What does it mean to be part of the body of Christ? What is my part in the body of Christ?
Respond
Lord, show me my spiritual gifts so that I may serve You, my buddies and Your mission. Amen.Day 2 — Sacrificial Service
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Romans 12:1-21
Reflect
In serving my country, I also want to serve my God. In order to serve, I need to know the mission. The mission is to do the will of God. How does Paul describe the will of God? What are some of the gifts God gives us? How should I act if Jesus is my Commander?
Respond
Lord, I serve You because I love You. Show me Your will and how my gifts and talents may contribute to Your mission. Amen.Day 1 — Aim High Pray: Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen. Read: Romans 8:1-39 Reflect We aim high because, once we belong to Christ, we are empowered with the Holy Spirit’s strength. We are free from the bondage of darkness and the shackles of sin. Freedom means momentum, and we are free to soar as high as the Holy Spirit allows. On what should we keep our minds focused? When we go through hard times, what promise does Paul offer us (v.28)? Can God do anything about our problems? Can anything separate us from the love of Christ? Respond Lord, I want to aim high. I want to join You in Your mission. Please show me the direction You want me to go. Amen.  ---- Each of our readers has a unique story of how they interact with the Bible. text.en: God began by calling a man, then a nation, and finally through Jesus, established a church. The Basic Training Challenge provides you with a starting point to learn about God’s mission here on earth through the Christian church. Similar to your basic training, this plan will challenge you to get spiritually fit in God’s Word.

When the Jewish rulers challenged the apostles for disobeying a direct order, what did Peter tell them? How did the apostles respond to being beaten for what they had done (vv.41-42)? How strong is your faith during tough times?
Respond
O Lord, I am weak, but You are strong. Help me through this time in my life. You alone are my Savior and my Lord. Amen.Day 3 — Board of Inquiry
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Acts 4:1-37
Reflect
Peter and the rest of the disciples were charged with teaching the people of Israel about Jesus. Their message was not always welcome, especially by Jewish priests and leaders. When the Jewish rulers challenged the apostles for disobeying a direct order, what did Peter tell them? How did the apostles respond to being beaten for what they had done (v.41-42)? How strong is my faith during tough times? How may I strengthen my faith?
Respond
I will continue to share the gospel of Jesus Christ even when to do so might cause me pain. Let my voice ring out in glory to Your son Jesus. Amen.Day 2 — Staging Area
Pray:
Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen.
Read: Acts 2:1-47
Reflect
What miraculous signs did God perform to show these Christians He was keeping His word? How did the crowd respond? What did Christ’s followers begin to do from then on (vv.43-47)? Which of these things are you doing today?
Respond
Lord Jesus, through the power of the Holy Spirit, help me to live as the first believers did: in prayer, in fellowship, in the Word and in the breaking of bread. Amen.Day 1 — Final Instructions Pray: Lord God, quiet my soul and open my mind and heart to receive Your Word. Amen. Read: Acts 1:1-14 Reflect Just before Jesus was taken up into heaven, He assured all the apostles that even though they did not know the timing, He would return and restore the Kingdom of Israel. He also assured them that the Holy Spirit would come to them and would provide guidance regarding what they should do. As Jesus was returning to heaven, what does He say will happen to His followers? What does He expect them to do? What does He expect us to do? Respond Heavenly Father, I will be Your disciple. I will be a witness for You with everyone, whether the time seems right or not. Amen. ---- Each of our readers has a unique story of how they interact with the Bible. We invite you to click on the link below, so we can learn more about you and readers like you. Your participation will help the American Bible Society continue to provide high-quality Bible resources for people everywhere and will inform the development of new Bible resources. Start Survey

text.en: The Bible doesn’t discuss leadership like a popular business book. However, since God is the creator of everything that exists as well as the rules and processes by which everything works, the Scriptures do provide principles and examples that give us insight and wisdom into effective leadership. The social and cultural backgrounds of the Bible are different than ours, but the Scriptures contain truth that transcends time and space.
